original_question: Let F be a non-abelian free pro-p group of finite rank. Can one find a finite collection U1,..., Un of open subgroups of F including F itself such that the only subgroup of F which is contained in Ui and is characteristic in Ui for every i is the trivial subgroup?
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially the paper’s official formulation, almost word for word: it has the right ambient object (a non-abelian free pro-p group of finite rank), the right existential quantifier (a finite collection of open subgroups), the requirement that F itself be included, and the correct conclusion that the only subgroup simultaneously contained in each Ui and characteristic in each Ui should be trivial.
missing_details: The prime p is implicit in the phrase "pro-p"; to make the question fully stand-alone, one can begin by fixing a prime p.
"Finite rank" is implicit shorthand for a finitely generated free pro-p group; equivalently, F has rank d>=2.
In the pro-p setting, "open subgroup" means open in the profinite topology on F.
To make the profinite meaning of "characteristic" explicit, one can say characteristic under all continuous automorphisms of Ui.

If one wants the question to be completely self-contained in profinite language, one may specify that the subgroup under discussion is a closed subgroup H<=F; this is standard but unstated in the notebook.
The existential quantifier is over a finite family depending on the given group F: for each such F, does there exist some finite family U1,...,Un with the stated property?
refined_question: Fix a prime p, and let F be a free pro-p group of finite rank d>=2. Does there exist a finite family of open subgroups U1,...,Un of F, with F among them, such that the only closed subgroup H<=F satisfying H<=Ui and H characteristic in Ui (with respect to continuous automorphisms) for every i=1,...,n is the trivial subgroup H=1?
justification: The arXiv item 1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, and your draft matches Problem 21.9 there essentially verbatim. The notebook gives no broader reformulation or equivalent version adjacent to this problem, so the faithful refinement is just a slight sharpening that makes the standard pro-p conventions explicit: the prime p is fixed, finite rank means finitely generated/non-abelian means rank at least 2, open is topological, and characteristic is interpreted in the profinite sense. No extra hypotheses should be added, and no broader commensurator-style reformulation appears in the notebook itself.
